AC9M4N01.title: Decimal Place Value: Tenths and Hundredths
AC9M4N01.curriculum: recognise and extend the application of place value to tenths and hundredths and use the conventions of decimal notation to name and represent decimals
AC9M4N01.routine: Build the whole → Partition into tenths → Partition into hundredths → Write decimal → Rename → Compare

misconceptions.correction: 0.75 is not automatically larger than 0.8; compare tenths first by writing 0.8 as 0.80.

misconceptions.misconception: Decimal point read as punctuation only
misconceptions.correction: The point separates whole-number and fractional place values.
Tenths are larger parts than hundredths: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths.
0.6 and 0.60 name the same quantity.

AC9M4N02.title: Properties of Odd and Even Numbers
AC9M4N02.curriculum: explain and use the properties of odd and even numbers
AC9M4N02.routine: Pair the quantity → Identify parity → Test an operation → Generalise → Justify

misconceptions.correction: Many odd numbers are composite, such as 9 and 15.
Odd × odd is odd.

misconceptions.misconception: A pattern from one example is proof
misconceptions.correction: Test several cases and explain using pairs or factors of 2.
Parity rules for subtraction match addition when whole-number results are allowed.

AC9M4N03.title: Equivalent Fractions and Decimal Connections
AC9M4N03.curriculum: find equivalent representations of fractions using related denominators and make connections between fractions and decimal notation
AC9M4N03.routine: Identify equal whole → Scale numerator and denominator → Verify model → Connect to tenths/hundredths → Compare

misconceptions.correction: Multiply or divide both numerator and denominator by the same non-zero factor.
Equivalent fraction models require equal-sized wholes.
Equivalent representations look different but have the same value.

AC9M4N04.title: Counting with Fractions and Mixed Numerals
AC9M4N04.curriculum: count by fractions including mixed numerals; locate and represent these fractions as numbers on number lines
AC9M4N04.routine: Choose step size → Partition each whole equally → Count beyond one → Rename → Locate and compare

misconceptions.correction: The denominator keeps naming the same-sized parts.
1 3/4 means one whole and three quarters, not 1 × 3/4.
Equal fraction steps require equal distances.
They are valid numbers greater than or equal to one.

AC9M4N05.title: Multiplying and Dividing by Multiples and Powers of 10
AC9M4N05.curriculum: solve problems involving multiplying or dividing natural numbers by multiples and powers of 10 without a calculator, using the multiplicative relationship between the place value of digits
AC9M4N05.routine: Identify factor or divisor → Track place-value shift → Calculate → Interpret units → Check inverse

misconceptions.correction: Place-value reasoning explains when and why placeholder zeros appear.
Remember the extra factor of 10.
Division by 10 makes each digit worth one tenth as much.
Interpret whether the answer counts items, cost, length or groups.

AC9M4N06.title: Efficient Calculation Strategies and Digital Tools
AC9M4N06.curriculum: develop efficient strategies and use appropriate digital tools for solving problems involving addition and subtraction, and multiplication and division where there is no remainder
AC9M4N06.routine: Estimate → Analyse numbers → Choose strategy/tool → Solve → Check → Compare efficiency

misconceptions.misconception: One method used for every problem
misconceptions.correction: Analyse the numbers before choosing a strategy.
Estimate and interpret the result.
Record every partitioned part before recombining.
A method should also be reliable and communicable.

AC9M4N07.title: Estimation, Rounding and Reasonableness
AC9M4N07.curriculum: choose and use estimation and rounding to check and explain the reasonableness of calculations including the results of financial transactions
AC9M4N07.routine: Identify purpose → Choose rounding level → Estimate → Calculate → Compare → Explain reasonableness

misconceptions.misconception: Always round to the same place
misconceptions.correction: Choose precision based on purpose.
Use approximately and distinguish estimate from exact result.
Rounding up may be more useful when checking whether money is sufficient.
An exact answer should be close to, not equal to, the estimate.

AC9M4N08.title: Mathematical Modelling in Multi-step Problems
AC9M4N08.curriculum: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving additive and multiplicative situations including financial contexts; formulate the problems using number sentences and choose efficient calculation strategies, using digital tools where appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation
AC9M4N08.routine: Understand context → Define quantities → Represent → Formulate operations → Solve → Validate → Communicate

misconceptions.correction: Include only quantities relevant to the question and model.
A mathematically cheaper option may not meet capacity, time or safety needs.
State what the result means in the situation.
Set up the mathematical relationship before using the tool.

AC9M4N09.title: Algorithms that Generate Number Sets
AC9M4N09.curriculum: follow and create algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions that use addition or multiplication to generate sets of numbers; identify and describe any emerging patterns
AC9M4N09.routine: Define input → Follow ordered steps → Apply decision → Record output set → Identify pattern → Test generalisation

misconceptions.correction: Algorithms depend on exact sequence.
Every possible outcome needs a defined next step.

misconceptions.misconception: Pattern stated from too few outputs
misconceptions.correction: Test enough inputs to support the description.
One describes how outputs change; the other links input directly to output.

AC9M4A01.title: Unknown Values in Addition and Subtraction Equations
AC9M4A01.curriculum: find unknown values in numerical equations involving addition and subtraction, using the properties of numbers and operations
AC9M4A01.routine: Read both sides → Identify unknown role → Preserve equality → Use inverse/property → Substitute and check

misconceptions.correction: It means both sides have equal value.

misconceptions.misconception: Same operation used regardless of unknown role
misconceptions.correction: Identify whether the missing value is an addend, minuend or subtrahend.
900 − 553 is not the same as 553 − 900.
Replace the box with the solution and evaluate both sides.

AC9M4A02.title: Multiplication Facts to 10 × 10 and Derived Strategies
AC9M4A02.curriculum: recall and demonstrate proficiency with multiplication facts up to 10 x 10 and related division facts; extend and apply facts to develop efficient mental strategies for computation with larger numbers without a calculator
AC9M4A02.routine: Recall core fact → Connect inverse → Use commutative/distributive relationship → Scale place value → Check

misconceptions.correction: Use facts as connected families, not isolated answers.
Add every partial product or quotient.
Identify the whole and known factor before selecting the inverse fact.
Subtract or add the exact adjustment after using a friendly fact.

AC9M4M01.title: Reading Scales, Partial Units and Digital Instruments
AC9M4M01.curriculum: interpret unmarked and partial units when measuring and comparing attributes of length, mass, capacity, duration and temperature, using scaled and digital instruments and appropriate units
AC9M4M01.routine: Identify attribute/unit → Read labelled endpoints → Count equal intervals → Find interval value → Read partial position → Record and compare

misconceptions.correction: Determine the spaces between labelled values.
Calculate the interval value from endpoints and number of intervals.
Convert to a common unit first.
State whether 02:35 means time of day or a duration, and include units.

AC9M4M02.title: Perimeter and Area of Shapes and Enclosed Spaces
AC9M4M02.curriculum: recognise ways of measuring and approximating the perimeter and area of shapes and enclosed spaces, using appropriate formal and informal units
AC9M4M02.routine: Identify boundary or surface → Choose unit → Measure/count → Calculate or approximate → Label units → Compare

misconceptions.correction: Ask whether the problem concerns around or covering.
Area uses square units such as cm².

misconceptions.misconception: Internal grid lines counted in perimeter
misconceptions.correction: Only the outer boundary contributes.
Use approximately and describe the method or range.

AC9M4M03.title: Duration, am/pm and Time Conversions
AC9M4M03.curriculum: solve problems involving the duration of time including situations involving “am” and “pm” and conversions between units of time
AC9M4M03.routine: Identify start/end → Mark am or pm → Bridge to friendly time → Add intervals → Convert units → Check context

misconceptions.correction: Use elapsed intervals; 1:10 − 9:35 is not ordinary place-value subtraction.
12:00 pm is noon and 12:00 am is midnight.

misconceptions.misconception: Minutes treated as hundredths of an hour
misconceptions.correction: An hour has 60 minutes.
Without it, a duration may be ambiguous.

AC9M4M04.title: Estimating and Comparing Angles
AC9M4M04.curriculum: estimate and compare angles using angle names including acute, obtuse, straight angle, reflex and revolution, and recognise their relationship to a right angle
AC9M4M04.routine: Identify vertex and arms → Compare with 90° → Compare with 180° → Name angle → Estimate turn → Justify

misconceptions.correction: Angle size depends on turn, not line length.

misconceptions.misconception: Reflex angle identified as smaller interior angle
misconceptions.correction: Specify which turn is being measured; reflex is the larger turn over 180°.
Rotating a diagram does not change the angle.

misconceptions.misconception: Straight angle called a line only
misconceptions.correction: A straight angle represents a half turn of 180°.

AC9M4SP01.title: Composite Shapes and Objects
AC9M4SP01.curriculum: represent and approximate composite shapes and objects in the environment, using combinations of familiar shapes and objects
AC9M4SP01.routine: Observe whole → Identify familiar components → Decompose → Represent → Approximate dimensions/position → Check resemblance

misconceptions.correction: Identify internal components and how they combine.
A drawing may use 2D shapes to represent a 3D object, but name both appropriately.
Relative size and position help the model resemble the object.
A model intentionally simplifies while preserving important features.

AC9M4SP02.title: Grid References, Directions and Pathways
AC9M4SP02.curriculum: create and interpret grid reference systems using grid references and directions to locate and describe positions and pathways
AC9M4SP02.routine: Orient grid → Read horizontal reference → Read vertical reference → Locate cell/point → Follow ordered directions → Verify endpoint

misconceptions.correction: State and follow the convention, usually column then row for letter–number cells.
Grid orientation remains fixed even after turns.

misconceptions.misconception: Moves counted by lines instead of cells
misconceptions.correction: Define whether a move crosses cells or grid intervals and apply consistently.

misconceptions.misconception: Cell reference and point coordinate mixed
misconceptions.correction: They locate different features unless the system defines otherwise.

AC9M4SP03.title: Line and Rotational Symmetry
AC9M4SP03.curriculum: recognise line and rotational symmetry of shapes and create symmetrical patterns and pictures, using dynamic geometric software where appropriate
AC9M4SP03.routine: Identify possible transformation → Test reflection/rotation → Check exact match → Count axes/order → Create and verify

misconceptions.correction: Symmetry requires exact correspondence.
Only lines that map the entire shape onto itself count.

misconceptions.misconception: 360° counted as the only rotational match
misconceptions.correction: Order includes all matching positions during one full turn, including the starting orientation.

misconceptions.misconception: Line and rotational symmetry assumed together
misconceptions.correction: A shape can have one without the other.

AC9M4ST01.title: Collecting and Representing Data with Many-to-One Displays
AC9M4ST01.curriculum: acquire data for categorical and discrete numerical variables to address a question of interest or purpose, using digital tools; represent data using many-to-one pictographs, column graphs and other displays or visualisations; interpret and discuss the information that has been created
AC9M4ST01.routine: Define question → Identify variable → Collect accurately → Organise digitally → Choose display/key/scale → Interpret → Discuss limitations

misconceptions.correction: Multiply symbols by the key value and interpret partial symbols proportionally.
Representation must match the source data exactly.
Collect a variable that directly addresses the purpose.
Describe what was collected without inventing causes.

AC9M4ST02.title: Comparing Data Displays and Distributions
AC9M4ST02.curriculum: analyse the effectiveness of different displays or visualisations in illustrating and comparing data distributions, then discuss the shape of distributions and the variation in the data
AC9M4ST02.routine: Identify question → Read scale/key → Describe concentration/gaps/extremes → Compare variation → Evaluate display → Support with data

misconceptions.correction: Read the axis scale and actual values.
Also discuss clusters, gaps and common values.
Investigate whether it is valid before excluding it.
Effectiveness depends on the question and audience.

AC9M4ST03.title: Conducting and Communicating Statistical Investigations
AC9M4ST03.curriculum: conduct statistical investigations, collecting data through survey responses and other methods; record and display data using digital tools; interpret the data and communicate the results
AC9M4ST03.routine: Pose question → Plan population/method → Collect ethically → Clean and organise → Display → Interpret → Communicate → Reflect

misconceptions.correction: Wording should not push respondents toward an answer.
Clean data before calculating frequencies.
State who was surveyed and limit the claim.
Let the question and data determine the display.

AC9M4P01.title: Likelihood, Outcomes and Independent or Dependent Events
AC9M4P01.curriculum: describe possible everyday events and the possible outcomes of chance experiments and order outcomes or events based on their likelihood of occurring; identify independent or dependent events
AC9M4P01.routine: Define experiment → List complete outcomes → Compare favourable outcomes → Order likelihood → Check replacement/conditions → Classify dependence

misconceptions.correction: A likely event can still fail to occur.
Use a systematic table or tree to include all ordered outcomes.
Independence concerns whether one event changes the chance of another.
State whether items are returned before the next draw.

AC9M4P02.title: Repeated Chance Experiments and Variation
AC9M4P02.curriculum: conduct repeated chance experiments to observe relationships between outcomes; identify and describe the variation in results
AC9M4P02.routine: Define outcomes → Predict → Conduct consistent trials → Record frequencies → Repeat/aggregate → Compare proportions → Describe variation

misconceptions.misconception: Equal chance means equal every run
misconceptions.correction: Small samples can vary considerably.
Record every valid trial, including surprising outcomes.
Use proportions or equal totals when comparing sets.

misconceptions.misconception: One trial used to judge fairness
misconceptions.correction: Repeated evidence is needed; even then conclusions should be cautious.
